title: Fallback to baseline kernels on quantization profile incompatibility (with metrics + structured logs)
author: Hiro Tanaka
description:
Context: As we roll out Quantization Profile Library support, some requests will resolve to a quantized profile that is not actually executable on the worker (GPU arch mismatch, missing kernel, invalid profile constraints for runtime version, or a conservative incompatibility check). Previously, several of these paths surfaced as hard errors (5xx) or ambiguous "profile not found" failures depending on where the mismatch was discovered. This PR makes incompatibility a non-fatal condition for request execution: the runtime will fall back to the baseline (non-quantized) kernel path when a resolved profile cannot be executed on the current worker, while emitting structured logs and metrics to make the behavior observable and debuggable.

Changes: (1) Introduce a single incompatibility decision point in the execution plan builder: once a profile is selected, we validate hardware scope + kernel availability + runtime compatibility; on any incompatibility we set execution_mode=baseline_fallback and continue with baseline kernels for that request. (2) Add explicit incompatibility reason codes and counters, segmented by model, profile_id, gpu_arch, and route_id (when present). (3) Add structured log event "quant_profile_incompatible_fallback" with reason, resolved profile metadata, worker GPU info, and request/route identifiers; logs are sampled to avoid volume spikes. (4) Ensure fallback is transparent to the request: the response includes normal content; we do not bubble incompatibility unless the caller explicitly requests debug headers (internal only). (5) Add guardrails for pathological cases: if baseline execution fails after fallback, we preserve the original error but include the fallback metadata to aid triage.

Reason codes (initial set): gpu_arch_not_in_scope, kernel_not_available, runtime_version_too_old, dtype_not_supported, seq_len_out_of_profile_bounds, kv_cache_layout_incompatible, unknown.

Notes: This PR intentionally does not change profile resolution policy (that is handled in the policy engine / routing layer). It only guarantees safe execution behavior at the runtime layer once a profile is provided/resolved. Also, this does not attempt a secondary profile selection; we fall back to baseline only. Follow-up work: optional "retry with alternate profile" once the library has multiple variants per model/hardware.

Testing: Added unit tests for reason mapping and plan selection, integration tests that simulate mismatched GPU arch and missing kernel bundles, and a load test in benchmark-lab to confirm fallback does not introduce latency regressions on the baseline path.

Rollout: Safe to deploy behind the existing quantization feature flag. Even with quant enabled for a route, this reduces risk by preventing incompatibility-induced 5xx and improves observability for library/profile curation.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added/updated [x] Integration tests added for incompatibility fallbacks [x] Metrics added + documented [x] Structured logs include no prompt/content [x] Backwards compatible (no API surface change) [x] Linked Linear issues updated

Related: ENG-18437 (profile fetch/cache), PR #28766 (fetch & cache profiles), PR #28792 (route policy enablement), ENG-18472 (telemetry tagging).
commits: runtime: centralize quant profile compatibility checks in execution planner
runtime: implement baseline fallback path + preserve original request context
obs: add quant_fallback_total and quant_incompat_reason_total counters
tests: add incompatibility fixtures + integration tests for missing kernels / arch mismatch
docs(internal): update runbook notes for quantization debugging signals
review_conversation:
Mateo Alvarez (review): Thanks for driving this. Two questions: (1) Are we sure we should always fall back (vs fail closed) for certain mismatches like seq_len_out_of_profile_bounds? (2) Can we guarantee we won’t log anything sensitive in the structured event? The event currently includes request_id and route_id which is fine, but please confirm no prompt text can leak via the error chain.

Hiro Tanaka (author): (1) Yes, for v1 we prefer availability over strictness. The profile bounds are advisory/validated for expected quality/perf, not correctness; falling back to baseline avoids breaking workloads that accidentally exceed bounds. I added an explicit comment and made seq_len_out_of_profile_bounds a distinct reason so we can alert/track if it’s common. (2) Confirmed: we never log input tokens/prompts. The event fields are constrained to ids + model/profile metadata + gpu info + reason. Also changed log to not include raw exception message (which could accidentally include config details) and instead include a safe error_code.

Noah Patel (review): Please ensure the fallback does not re-run the same compatibility check twice (I see validateProfileCompatibility is invoked in both resolve() and plan_builder). Also, we should avoid a stampede on kernel bundle lookup when missing.

Hiro Tanaka (author): Good catch. I removed the earlier resolve() check and made plan_builder the single source of truth. For kernel lookups, we now cache negative lookups for 60s in the local kernel registry, so repeated misses don’t cause repeated remote checks.

Mina Haddad (review): For metrics cardinality: tagging by route_id and profile_id is useful but can explode. Can we gate route_id to only when present + hashed? Also ensure we have a sane default in Hosted where route_id may be unset.

Hiro Tanaka (author): Updated metrics to include route_id only when it’s a stable internal id (not customer-provided), and we hash it before export. If route_id is missing we emit route_id=unknown. profile_id remains since the library is Redwood-published and bounded.

Logan Wright (review): Can you add a companion histogram for added latency due to fallback? Even if minimal, it would help confirm there is no hidden overhead.

Hiro Tanaka (author): Added quant_fallback_plan_overhead_ms (timer around compatibility + replan), plus quant_execution_mode tag on existing request latency metric. The overhead stays sub-millisecond in integration.

Sean Gallagher (review): From SRE perspective: please make sure fallback is visible in error budgets / alerts but not paging by default. I’d like an alert that triggers only when fallback rate spikes (e.g., >1% for 10m) for a given model/profile.

Hiro Tanaka (author): Added a proposed alert query to the internal doc and confirmed with Allison that we can implement in the quantization dashboard pack. No paging by default; warning-level.

Mateo Alvarez (final): LGTM after the cardinality fix and the removal of duplicate checks.

Noah Patel (final): Approved.

Mina Haddad (final): Approved.

Logan Wright (final): Approved.

Sean Gallagher (final): Approved.
release_notes: Runtime now safely falls back to baseline execution when a quantization profile is incompatible with the current worker/hardware. Adds reason-coded metrics and structured logs to diagnose profile/hardware mismatches without causing request failures.
